text: Across multiple ResNet depths and VGG-13/16/19 transforms, ETTs consistently outperform the alternative pruning-at-initialization methods SNIP and GraSP, particularly at high sparsities.

On ImageNet at sparsity (fraction of zero weights) 73.79%, Elastic Ticket Transformation (ETT)-transferred tickets for ResNet architectures attain top-1 accuracies close to Iterative Magnitude-based Pruning (IMP)-found tickets and substantially above the pruning-at-initialization baselines SNIP and GraSP.

Across CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments, transferred tickets produced by Elastic Ticket Transformations (ETTs) substantially outperform the state-of-the-art pruning-at-initialization methods SNIP and GraSP and one-shot magnitude pruning baselines at matched sparsity levels (fraction of zero weights).

When transferring winning tickets across ResNet depths, one should choose residual blocks as the minimal replication unit for ResNets, and a convolutional layer plus normalization layer as the minimal replication unit for VGG, consistent with model structure.

For the VGG variants VGG-13-2, VGG-13-3, and VGG-13-5, differing in numbers of fully-connected (FC) layers, and for multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) of varying widths on MNIST, the Elastic Lottery Ticket Hypothesis approach (E-LTH) transfers at 89.26% sparsity (fraction of zero weights) with ≤0.21% accuracy differences relative to directly trained winning tickets.
